name: lipgloss-77047a83-blind30
instr:
# lipgloss-regen

An application built on this library lays out formatted text for a character-cell screen, and it now both mismeasures and misdraws that text in a number of places. Nothing about the callers changed and nothing about the data changed. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits.

Start with the simplest question anyone asks it: how much room does something need. Asking how many lines a finished block occupies comes back two too low — a single-line string reports minus one, and a block filled out to twenty lines of content reports eighteen — so anything laid out to a fixed number of lines ends up the wrong shape, and a grid capped to six lines does not measure six when its cells are told not to break their text. The vertical room attributed to a frame's lower edge is reported as two lines rather than one, so any layout that subtracts frame room from the space available reserves too much. Asking for a run of five filler characters hands back six. A block given inner spacing and a frame and then told to occupy a given number of columns measures one column too many, because the long horizontal line of the upper and lower edges runs one character past its end; that happens even when the vertical edges are switched off and only those two are drawn. And bringing a grid down to eighty columns when every cell carries a wide outer gap on both sides apportions the columns badly, mishandling a column that is already down to the least it can take; long mixe
